title: Security deposit transfer to new owner and withholding penalties (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21)
requirement: When a property is sold, the new owner must obtain the tenant's security deposit plus accrued interest and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest, and returning it. Willfully withholding deposits of tenants who receive State or federal rental assistance triggers a civil penalty.
coverage_conditions: All residential landlord-tenant relationships; the packet states no building-size or building-age limit for the security deposit rules.

applicability.per_tenancy: Higher penalties apply when the tenant receives State or federal financial or rental assistance.

penalty: Civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense for willfully withholding an assisted tenant's deposit; unlawful use of deposit monies is a disorderly persons offense with a fine of not less than $200 or up to 30 days' imprisonment, or both.
quoted_span: Whether or not the deposit and interest are transferred, t he new owner is responsible for the investment of the security deposit, giving all notices and paying interest, and for the return of the security deposit, plus any accrued earnings or interest (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21).

title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1)
requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a residential dwelling unit only with the tenant's consent or through the legal eviction process, and may not evict or fail to renew a lease without good cause proven in court. A Notice to Quit is required for good-cause evictions other than nonpayment.
coverage_conditions: All residential landlords and dwelling units used as a residence; the packet states no building-size or building-age limit.
quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law rent control exemption (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5)
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control or rent leveling ordinance for 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings; exempt from local rent control for 30 years after construction is completed.

coverage_quotes: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years after completion; rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control.
quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

title: Anti-Eviction Act rent increase notice and unconscionability (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1)
requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease; to increase rent the landlord must terminate the old lease, give proper written notice, and offer a new lease at the increased rent. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances.
coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies; before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent the landlord must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
quoted_span: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased rental payment.

relations.quote: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

title: Conversion rent increase restriction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31)
requirement: If a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still be raised to cover new services or amenities.
coverage_conditions: All tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, regardless of eligibility for protected tenancy.
exemptions: Rent increases to cover the cost of new services or amenities are not barred.
quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

title: Law Against Discrimination source-of-lawful-income protection (N.J.S.A. 10:5-12)
requirement: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination prohibits a landlord or rental agency from discriminating in renting housing based on a person's source of lawful income, among other protected classes, and requires equal treatment.
coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships, except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences (as to familial status).

conditions.text: rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home
residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex

coverage_quotes: The law applies to all landlord -tenant relationships, except those involving two -family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident -occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age -restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status (N.J.S.A. 10:5-5(n)).

exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex (YMCA and age-restricted housing), as to familial status.
penalty: Landlords who violate the LAD are subject to fines and penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense.
quoted_span: discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: Credit report screening and adverse-action notice
requirement: A landlord may obtain and use a prospective tenant's credit report in deciding whether to rent; if the application is denied because of the report, the landlord must give the applicant the name, address and telephone number of the credit reporting or screening agency that supplied it.
coverage_conditions: Prospective tenants screened by landlords using credit reports or tenant screening agencies.
quoted_span: If a tenant's  application is denied due their credit report, the landlord must provide the tenant with the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or screening agency that supplied the negative report (15 U.S.C.A. § 1681m).

title: Permitted tenant screening and application charges
requirement: A landlord may charge a tenant or applicant for the cost of a credit or screening report and may request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
coverage_conditions: Rental applicants screened by landlords; the packet states no cap on the amount that may be charged.
quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
